La Global Sumud Flotilla n’a pas atteint: The Global Sumud Flotilla never reached Gaza, but the arrests and the testimonies have revived the debate over the blockade and solidarity.

<strong>Les bateaux n’ont jamais atteint: The boats never reached Gaza. Yet for many of those who took part in the Global Sumud Flotilla or followed it from Gaza and Montréal, the heart of its mission may not have been on the water. Through the testimonies of a Canadian activist who has returned from the mission, a Palestinian woman in Montréal and a journalist speaking from a bombing zone, another question emerges: can a flotilla still change anything when it doesn’t deliver its aid?
À travers les témoignages d’une militant: Through the testimonies of a Canadian activist who has returned from the mission, a Palestinian woman in Montréal and a journalist in Gaza, our report explores one question: can a flotilla still change anything when it doesn’t reach its destination?
La vidéo a fait le tour du monde. On y v: The video travelled around the world. In it, activists from the Global Sumud Flotilla kneel face down on the ground, hands bound behind their backs, surrounded by soldiers of the Israel Defense Forces (IDF) during their detention. A few hours earlier, their boats had been intercepted in international waters, and the activists were arrested and transferred to Israeli warships headed for the port of Ashdod. The images, released by Israeli National Security Minister Itamar Ben-Gvir, quickly set off a wave of outrage and international criticism of Tel Aviv. Several countries, including Spain, France, Italy, Great Britain and the Netherlands, condemned “a violation of human dignity.” Canada’s Foreign Affairs Minister Anita Anand, whose country had 12 nationals in the flotilla, condemned “inhumane treatment” and “heinous abuses for which those responsible must be held to account.”
« Toutes les techniques de torture ont é: “Every torture technique was used on all of the participants,” says Safa Chebbi. “There were fractures, there were really serious injuries; some people are still in hospital. And there were also sexual assaults against men and women,” she told La Converse. The testimonies will be documented in a detailed report that will soon be made public, she promises, and that report will be used to drag Israel before a court.
Nous l’avons rencontrée chez elle à Mont: We met her at her home in Montréal. Two days after returning to Canada, Safa Chebbi still bears the marks of deep exhaustion, a few bruises she brushes off, and a calm, distant smile, that of someone coming back from a battle without yet having fully left the field behind. Among the powerful images she retains from her detention are the marks left on the cell walls by Palestinian detainees: “It carried a lot of pain and love at the same time. You also saw traces of violence, traces of blood on the walls. The cell truly speaks of the violence experienced by Palestinians and prisoners in those spaces.”
La flotte de la Global Sumud comprenait: The Global Sumud fleet initially comprised 58 boats and thousands of participants from 56 countries. Starting on May 18, the Israeli navy began boarding them off the coast of Cyprus. In the end,<l1> 50 boats were intercepted, and 426 activists were arrested and detained</l1> in Israeli prisons.
Ses initiateurs qualifient la flottille: Its organizers describe the flotilla as “the largest coordinated civilian maritime operation ever undertaken in Palestine.” It set out with a clear goal: to deliver humanitarian aid to Gaza and try to break the<l1> blockade imposed on the Palestinian territory, which is pushing its population into famine and has been widely denounced, including by the Canadian government</l1>.
Israël justifie ces interceptions par de: Israel justifies the interceptions on security grounds and defends the legality of the maritime blockade imposed on Gaza.
« Israël a pleinement le droit d’empêche: “Israel has every right to prevent provocative flotillas of Hamas terrorist supporters from entering our territorial waters and reaching Gaza,” Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu said in a social media post.
Rapellons que l’armée israelienne a inte: Let us recall that the Israeli army intercepted the flotilla’s boats more than 400 km from Gaza. In a <l1>joint statement</l1> published on May 18, the foreign ministers of Spain, Turkey, Bangladesh, Brazil, Colombia, Jordan, Libya, Malaysia, the Maldives, Pakistan and South Africa called the seizure of the boats in international waters a “flagrant violation of international humanitarian law.”
Les autorités israéliennes rejettent éga: Israeli authorities also reject accusations that Gaza is being deprived of humanitarian aid. “The Gaza Strip is flooded with aid,” said Israeli Foreign Minister Gideon Sa'ar, claiming that more than 1.58 million tonnes of humanitarian aid had entered the enclave since October 2025.
Ces affirmations sont toutefois contesté: These claims are nonetheless disputed by several international humanitarian organizations and UN bodies, which continue to sound the alarm about the food and health situation in the Palestinian enclave.
De leur côté, les militants de la flotil: For their part, the flotilla activists maintain that the mission goes beyond food aid. For those we put the question to (see our video), the answer is measured not only in tonnes of food or boxes of medicine, but also in the visibility created for the Palestinian cause. “Obviously, it’s a maritime, civilian and humanitarian mission. Its goal is to bring humanitarian aid to Gaza, break the siege and open a humanitarian corridor for aid,” explains Safa Chebbi. “But breaking the siege isn’t only a humanitarian or geographic mission. It’s also political, diplomatic and media-related.”
Elle poursuit : « Notre rôle, c’est auss: She continues: “Our role is also to break the silence around a siege that has existed against Gaza for almost 20 years. Our goal is to put Palestine back at the centre of international news once again.”
<strong>À Gaza, une guerre qui continue<: In Gaza, a war that goes on
Pendant que les militants rentraient che: While the activists were heading home, Issa Saadallah spoke with us from Jabaliya, in northern Gaza. A journalist for 26 years, he has not left the enclave since the war began in October 2023.
Quelle est la situation en ce moment à G: What is the situation in Gaza right now? To that first question, he answers almost nonchalantly: “About ten minutes ago, an Israeli bombing targeted a group of civilians about a hundred metres from here. I don’t have the details yet because I logged on to speak with you.”
Puis, il reprend : « La situation est ac: Then he continues: “The situation is currently at its most critical point in 32 months of ongoing crisis. A tragic situation. Most people are living in tents. The water isn’t drinkable, the food isn’t fit for consumption, the health system is completely destroyed, the education system is in ruins.”
Il raconte aussi les premiers mois du si: He also recounts the first months of the siege: “For about six months, we were forced to eat animal feed, sometimes spoiled. We ate grass. We drank stagnant water and held our noses to be able to swallow it.”
Dans ce contexte, il reconnaît lui-même: Against this backdrop, he himself acknowledges the material limits of a flotilla’s aid. “Even if it reaches Gaza, it only brings a few items.” He immediately adds a nuance, however: “These movements express global powerlessness. The powerlessness of governments, of European countries, of Arab countries, of countries around the world.”

Abuses documented by Francesca Albanese, the United Nations Special Rapporteur on the situation of human rights in the Palestinian territories occupied since 1967.

Chebbi puts that figure in the context of the war on Gaza: “The genocide has been going on for three years, and the outrage is still selective.” For her, the flotilla existed because governments failed. That is when people organize and take on their responsibilities. “The role of the peoples of the Global North is to use their privilege, to use their bodies to face a war machine and make the reality of Palestinians visible.”
Cette lecture se rapproche d’une réflexi: This reading echoes a broader reflection on international solidarity movements: if institutions seem unable to change a situation, some citizens seek to act on their own.
Lors d’une<l1> soirée dialogue</l1>, La: At a<l1> dialogue evening</l1>, La Converse gauged the frustration of Palestinians living in Montréal over the neglect of their pain and the violence raging in their homeland. Among them, Reem Majid follows recent events from another position: that of a Palestinian woman living far from Gaza, but who sees the war permeate the daily lives of thousands of people here as well.
Membre du mouvement Palestinian Youth Mo: A member of the Palestinian Youth Movement (PYM), she has taken part since the start of the war in demonstrations and solidarity campaigns organized in the city.
Pour elle, les flottilles sont apparues: For her, the flotillas emerged in a particular context: that of a popular mobilization that has grown without, in her view, getting the response expected from Western governments. “We can see that the West rose up in response to this genocide, protested and brought people into the streets, but people saw that it wasn’t enough.” Then she adds: “People wanted to take matters into their own hands and offer aid themselves, because Western governments weren’t doing it.”
Reem Majid estime que le rôle des flotti: Reem Majid believes the role of the flotillas goes beyond their immediate humanitarian function, and also carries another idea: that of an international mobilization that continues despite repeated interceptions and the support some states continue to give Israel. “The flotilla is a sign that people around the world, particularly people of conscience around the world, continue to fight against the Israeli regime,” she says, “despite the fact that their governments support it.” She also sees it as a way for some citizens to take a public stand: “People keep saying that they refuse to be complicit [...] and that they support Palestinians.”
Depuis Montréal, son regard reprend une: From Montréal, her perspective takes up a question that runs through all the testimonies we gathered: when institutions seem unable to act, how far can citizens take over?
Issa Saadallah dit ne pas avoir été surp: Issa Saadallah says he was not surprised by recent events. Since the blockade was imposed on Gaza in 2007, several flotillas have been intercepted by Israel, sometimes violently. He mentions in particular the Mavi Marmara in 2010, when nine Turkish activists were killed during an Israeli assault.
Mais ce qui le frappe davantage est la f: But what strikes him more is the weakness of the international reactions. “I was surprised by the modest global reaction, particularly the European reaction.”
Pour lui, les condamnations diplomatique: For him, diplomatic condemnations remain largely symbolic. “All they do is summon an ambassador to protest or reprimand him.” He believes this lack of concrete consequences risks encouraging Israel to go further. “It’s a signal that allows Israel to attack again and encourages attacks on anyone who tries to help the Palestinian people.”
Puis il élargit sa réflexion aux flottil: Then he widens his reflection to the flotillas themselves. In his eyes, their immediate impact necessarily remains limited against the international balance of power. “The result is relative. Even if it’s modest, I think that in the long or medium term there will be a positive result.”
Il évoque l’effet cumulatif des réseaux: He points to the cumulative effect of social media, images and citizen mobilizations that continue to fuel a gradual shift in Western public opinion. “Even a large part of the American people are very unhappy with Israeli crimes. There are also European peoples who are not satisfied with what is happening and they find these means of solidarity.”
Mais cette solidarité reste traversée pa: But this solidarity remains marked by a deep contradiction, because, as he sums it up, “the flotillas express global powerlessness: the powerlessness of governments, of European countries, of Arab countries, of countries around the world.”
Même si une flottille atteint Gaza, dit-: Even if a flotilla reaches Gaza, he says, its cargo remains derisory compared with the scale of the needs. Its real function would therefore lie elsewhere: in its ability to keep Gaza visible and to create, despite everything, a space for international solidarity. “The least they can do is organize such maritime missions to express their solidarity and ease their conscience,” he says, speaking of citizens who refuse to remain passive in the face of “children killed, burned alive,” prisoners “tortured to death” and a population “completely besieged.”
Depuis Jabaliya, dans le nord de l’encla: From Jabaliya, in the north of the Palestinian enclave, Issa Saadallah also sends a message to the Canadian prime minister. “What you wouldn’t accept happening to your children and grandchildren under the Canadian banner, don’t accept it happening to Palestinian children,” he says. Then he adds: “I hope he will take a position that will ease his conscience and that of humanity.”
La Global Sumud Flotilla n’a pas atteint: The Global Sumud Flotilla did not reach the Palestinian enclave, like several missions before it. But for those who took part in it or watched it from Gaza and Montréal, its main cargo may not have been only in the boats.
Dans les jours suivant l’interception, l: In the days after the interception, the images of the arrests, and then those of the activists being welcomed home in their countries, put Gaza back in the spotlight, after the enclave had been largely eclipsed by the conflict between the United States and Iran.
Et pendant que les débats diplomatiques: And while the diplomatic debates drag on,<l1> the death toll keeps rising too</l1>.
Depuis 2008, plusieurs flottilles civile: Since 2008, several international civilian flotillas have tried to reach Gaza to challenge the blockade imposed by Israel since 2007 and deliver humanitarian aid.
Les premières missions du mouvement <em>: The first missions of the Free Gaza movement managed to reach the Palestinian enclave in 2008. But the most notable episode came in 2010 with the Mavi Marmara, a Turkish ship stormed by the Israeli army in international waters. Nine activists were killed, triggering a major diplomatic crisis between Israel and Turkey.
Depuis, plusieurs autres missions mariti: Since then, several other maritime missions, such as the Freedom Flotilla, the Women’s Boat to Gaza in 2016, and the Handala expedition in September 2025, have been intercepted, with their participants arrested and then deported. The Global Sumud Flotilla is the 38<sup>th</sup> expedition in the tradition of naval solidarity with Gaza.
Au fil des années, les flottilles sont d: Over the years, the flotillas have become as much political and media actions as humanitarian operations, aimed at keeping Gaza in international attention and denouncing the Israeli blockade.

**SEO Summary :** Interceptée avant d’at: **SEO Summary:** Intercepted before reaching Gaza, the Global Sumud Flotilla was unable to deliver its humanitarian aid. Yet according to the testimonies of a Canadian activist, a Palestinian woman in Montréal and a journalist in Gaza, its impact goes beyond the cargo it carried. Arrests, allegations of mistreatment, international criticism and citizen mobilization are reviving the debate over the Gaza blockade, the role of governments and the ability of solidarity movements to keep the Palestinian crisis at the heart of global attention.
